rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier people of that age disputed resurrection and the Hour; more than one early authority is said to report this doubt.
rows.anchor: ذكر غير واحد من السلف أنه كان قد حصل لأهل ذلك الزمان شك في البعث

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: A group held that souls would be raised but bodies would not; God made the Sleepers a proof and sign against that view.
rows.anchor: وقال عكرمة: كان منهم طائفة قد قالوا: تبعث الأرواح ولا تبعث الأجساد.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When one sleeper went to buy food in the city he found its people and landmarks transformed; his old coinage drew suspicion, and he said he remembered the city under Diocletian the previous evening.
rows.anchor: فلما رآها ذلك الرجل أنكرها وأنكر ضربها، فدفعها إلى جاره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed poet is cited to contrast familiar dwellings with inhabitants changed beyond recognition.
rows.anchor: أما الديار فإنها كديارهم … وأرى رجال الحي غير رجاله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account says the returning sleeper asked to enter first to tell his companions, but people did not know how he disappeared and God concealed what happened.
rows.anchor: فيقال: إنهم لا يدرون كيف ذهب فيه، وأخفى الله عليهم خبره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account says the people entered, and the Muslim ruler Tydosis greeted and embraced the sleepers; they spoke with him, returned to their resting places, and God caused them to die.
rows.anchor: وكان مسلما فيما قيل، واسمه تيدوسيس

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, campaigning with Habib ibn Maslama in Byzantine territory, saw bones in a cave; he said the Sleepers' bones had decayed after more than three hundred years. Ibn Jarir transmits it.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: غزا (4) ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As God first caused the Sleepers to lie down and then woke them in their recognizable forms, He exposed them to that generation as proof of resurrection for believers and deniers alike.
rows.anchor: أي: كما أرقدناهم وأيقظناهم بهيآتهم، أطلعنا عليهم أهل ذلك الزمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The suggestion to build over them means sealing the cave entrance and leaving them as they were.
rows.anchor: أي: سدوا عليهم باب كهفهم، وذروهم على حالهم

rows.speaker: ابن جرير
rows.claim: Two views identify those who proposed building a mosque: the believers among them, or the polytheists; Ibn Kathir leaves the matter to God.
rows.anchor: حكى ابن جرير في القائلين (6) ذلك قولين: أحدهما: إنهم المسلمون منهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The proposal came from people with authority, but whether it deserves praise is doubtful in light of the Prophet's warning against turning prophets' and righteous people's graves into mosques.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن الذين قالوا ذلك هم أصحاب الكلمة والنفوذ. ولكن هل هم محمودون أم لا؟ فيه نظر

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet cursed Jews and Christians for taking the graves of their prophets and righteous people as mosques, warning against that practice.
rows.anchor: لعن الله اليهود والنصارى، اتخذوا قبور أنبيائهم وصالحيهم مساجد

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: When Umar found Daniel's grave in Iraq, he ordered it hidden from people and a scroll found with it, containing prophecies and other material, buried.
rows.anchor: أنه لما وجد قبر دانيال في زمانه بالعراق، أمر أن يخفى عن الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When resolving to do something later, the Messenger is taught to make it conditional on God's will: God knows the unseen, what occurred and will occur, and even what would have happened had it not happened.
rows.anchor: أن يرد ذلك إلى مشيئة الله، عز وجل، علام الغيوب، الذي يعلم ما كان وما يكون

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet reports that Solomon vowed to visit seventy women that night, with narrations giving ninety or one hundred; an angel told him to say God willing, but he did not, and only one woman bore half a person.
rows.anchor: لأطوفن الليلة على سبعين امرأة -وفي رواية تسعين امرأة. وفي رواية: مائة امرأة

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet said that had Solomon said God willing, he would not have broken his oath and would have attained his wish, with all sons becoming horsemen for God's cause.
rows.anchor: لو قال: "إن شاء الله" لم يحنث، وكان دركا لحاجته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage was also revealed after the Prophet promised to answer a question about the Sleepers the next day; revelation was delayed fifteen days, as recounted earlier in the sura.
rows.anchor: لما سئل عن قصة أصحاب الكهف: "غدا أجيبكم". فتأخر الوحي خمسة عشر يوما

rows.speaker: أبو العالية والحسن البصري
rows.claim: They interpret remembering the Lord after forgetting as remembering to add the exception, then saying it when one recalls.
rows.anchor: قيل: معناه إذا نسيت الاستثناء، فاستثن عند ذكرك له. قاله أبو العالية، والحسن البصري.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A person who swears may add an exception even up to a year later; Ibn Abbas applied the verse to this, in a report transmitted through Mujahid and al-A'mash from Layth ibn Abi Sulaym.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد، عن ابن عباس في الرجل يحلف؟ قال: له أن يستثني ولو إلى سنة

rows.speaker: ابن جرير
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas means that one who forgot to say God willing may say it when remembering, even a year later and after breaking the oath; this renews the recommended practice but does not remove the breach or its expiation. Ibn Kathir calls this correct.
rows.anchor: لا أن يكون [ذلك] (6) رافعا لحنث اليمين ومسقطا للكفارة. وهذا الذي قاله ابن جرير، رحمه الله، هو الصحيح

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima reads remembering the Lord after forgetting as remembering when angry; Ibn Kathir calls this an interpretation by necessary implication.
rows.anchor: وقال عكرمة: {واذكر ربك إذا نسيت} أي: إذا غضبت. وهذا تفسير باللازم.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Two al-Tabarani reports explain the instruction as remembering to say God willing: one comes through Jabir ibn Zayd and one through Mujahid.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس: {ولا تقولن لشيء إني فاعل ذلك غدا إلا أن يشاء الله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A further report says the instruction to add the exception when remembered was specific to the Prophet; others may only qualify an oath in connection with making it. Al-Tabarani notes this route is unique through al-Walid ibn Muslim from Abd al-Aziz ibn al-Husayn.
rows.anchor: وروى الطبراني، أيضا عن ابن عباس في قوله: {واذكر ربك إذا نسيت} الاستثناء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another possible reading is to remember God whenever one forgets something in speech: forgetfulness begins with Satan, as in the attendant's explanation of forgetting the fish, while God's remembrance drives Satan away and brings recollection.
rows.anchor: النسيان منشؤه من الشيطان، كما قال فتى موسى: {وما أنسانيه إلا الشيطان أن أذكره}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When asked about something unknown, ask God and turn to Him for help in reaching the soundest guidance; Ibn Kathir notes that other interpretations were also given without detailing them.
rows.anchor: وقوله: {وقل عسى أن يهدين ربي لأقرب من هذا رشدا} أي: إذا سئلت عن شيء لا تعلمه، فاسأل الله فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God reports that the Sleepers remained three hundred lunar years plus nine, which equals three hundred solar years because each century differs by three years in the two calendars.
rows.anchor: وأنه كان مقداره ثلاثمائة [سنة] (6) وتسع سنين بالهلالية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without revealed knowledge or instruction about their duration, one must not speculate but say God knows; only God, or someone He informs, knows the unseen. Ibn Kathir says this is also the view of many early and later exegetes, including Mujahid.
rows.anchor: فلا تتقدم فيه بشيء، بل قل في مثل هذا: {الله أعلم بما لبثوا

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada, followed by Mutarrif ibn Abd Allah, says the three hundred years plus nine was the People of the Book's statement, rejected by the following command to say God knows; he cites a variant reading attributed to Ibn Masud, وقالوا ولبثوا.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة في قوله: {ولبثوا في كهفهم ثلاث مائة سنين وازدادوا تسعا} هذا قول أهل الكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir rejects Qatada's attribution: the People of the Book give three hundred solar years without nine; the verse is God's own report, as Ibn Jarir also chose. The Ibn Masud reading has a disconnected transmission and is anomalous against the majority reading, so it is not evidence.
rows.anchor: وظاهر من الآية إنما هو إخبار من الله، لا حكاية عنهم. وهذا اختيار ابن جرير، رحمه الله.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means God sees and hears them. Ibn Jarir treats it as emphatic praise: God sees every existing thing and hears every audible thing, with nothing hidden from Him.
rows.anchor: ما أبصره وأسمعه، وتأويل الكلام: ما أبصر الله لكل موجود، وأسمعه لكل مسموع

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says no one sees more clearly or hears better than God.
rows.anchor: ثم روي عن قتادة في قوله: {أبصر به وأسمع} فلا أحد أبصر (3) من الله ولا أسمع

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says God sees people's deeds and hears them, being all-hearing and all-seeing.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: {أبصر به وأسمع} يرى أعمالهم، ويسمع ذلك منهم سميعا بصيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone possesses creation and command; no one can overturn His judgment, and He has no minister, helper, partner, or adviser.
rows.anchor: أي: أنه تعالى هو الذي له الخلق والأمر، الذي لا معقب لحكمه، وليس له وزير ولا نصير ولا شريك ولا مشير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Messenger is commanded to recite and convey God's Book; its words cannot be changed, distorted, or reinterpreted away.
rows.anchor: بتلاوة كتابه العزيز وإبلاغه (2) إلى الناس: {لا مبدل لكلماته}

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid glosses a refuge as a place of shelter; Qatada glosses it as a protector or master.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد: {ملتحدا} قال: ملجأ. وعن قتادة: وليا ولا مولى

rows.speaker: ابن جرير
rows.claim: Ibn Jarir explains that if Muhammad failed to recite what was revealed, he would have no refuge from God; conveying the message is reinforced by the command in 5:67 and the warning in 28:85.
rows.anchor: إن أنت يا محمد لم تتل ما أوحي إليك من كتاب ربك، فإنه لا ملجأ لك من الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet should sit with people who remember, praise, glorify, and invoke God morning and evening, regardless of whether they are poor or rich, strong or weak.
rows.anchor: مع الذين يذكرون الله ويهللونه، ويحمدونه ويسبحونه ويكبرونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is said that Quraysh notables asked the Prophet to meet them alone and separate from poor companions such as Bilal, Ammar, Suhayb, Khabbab, and Ibn Masud; God instead commanded him to remain with them, as in 6:52.
rows.anchor: يقال: إنها نزلت في أشراف قريش، حين طلبوا من النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أن يجلس معهم وحده

rows.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص
rows.claim: Sa'd recounts that six companions were with the Prophet when polytheists demanded that he dismiss them; he felt what God willed, and this verse forbidding their expulsion was revealed. Muslim alone transmits it.
rows.anchor: قال: كنا مع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ستة نفر، فقال المشركون للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: اطرد هؤلاء

rows.speaker: أبو أمامة
rows.claim: The Prophet told a preacher to continue, saying that sitting from morning until sunrise listening to him was dearer than freeing four people.
rows.anchor: قص، فلأن أقعد غدوة إلى أن تشرق الشمس، أحب إلي من أن أعتق أربع رقاب

rows.speaker: رجل من أصحاب بدر
rows.claim: A man from the veterans of Badr heard the Prophet say that sitting in a preacher's gathering was dearer to him than freeing four people; Ahmad transmits the report through Kurdus.
rows.anchor: أخبرني رجل من أصحاب بدر: أنه سمع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: "لأن أقعد في مثل هذا المجلس أحب إلي من أن أعتق أربع رقاب".

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك
rows.claim: The Prophet preferred sitting with people remembering God from dawn prayer to sunrise over everything the sun shines on, and remembrance from afternoon prayer to sunset over freeing eight descendants of Ishmael, each valued at twelve thousand; Anas corrects a report that says four, totaling their value as ninety-six thousand.
rows.anchor: لأن أجالس قوما يذكرون الله من صلاة الغداة (13) إلى طلوع الشمس، أحب إلي مما طلعت عليه الشمس

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: When the Prophet passed a man reciting the Cave or Hijr and the man stopped, he said this was the gathering in which he had been commanded to remain patiently; al-Bazzar gives both a disconnected route and a connected version from Abu Hurayra and Abu Sa'id.
rows.anchor: هذا المجلس الذي أمرت أن أصبر نفسي معهم

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك
rows.claim: A group who gather to remember God seeking only His face are called from heaven to rise forgiven, with their bad deeds changed into good; Ahmad alone transmits this report.
rows.anchor: ما من قوم اجتمعوا يذكرون الله، لا يريدون بذلك إلا وجهه، إلا ناداهم مناد من السماء: أن قوموا مغفورا لكم

rows.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن سهل بن حنيف
rows.claim: When this verse came while the Prophet was at home, he sought out rough, poorly clothed people remembering God, sat with them, and praised God for making such people part of his community; al-Tabarani transmits the report.
rows.anchor: فخرج يلتمسهم، فوجد قوما يذكرون الله تعالى، منهم ثائر الرأس، وجافي الجلد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Dawud listed Abd al-Rahman as a Companion, while his father was among the leading Companions.
rows.anchor: عبد الرحمن هذا، ذكره أبو بكر بن أبي داود في الصحابة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Do not look past the poor worshippers toward others in search of people with social rank and wealth.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: ولا تجاوزهم إلى غيرهم: يعني: تطلب بدلهم أصحاب الشرف والثروة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heedless person is occupied with worldly life instead of religion and worship; his affairs are folly, neglect, and waste, so do not obey, love, or envy his way. The warning recalls not coveting worldly adornment in 20:131.
rows.anchor: أي: شغل عن الدين وعبادة ربه بالدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The message brought by Muhammad is the certain truth from God; the choice to believe or disbelieve is a severe threat, and the wrongdoers meant here are those who reject God, His Messenger, and His Book. The fire's enclosure is its wall.
rows.anchor: هذا من باب التهديد والوعيد الشديد؛ ولهذا قال

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet said Hell's enclosure has four walls, each extending forty years in thickness or distance; Ahmad reports it, and Tirmidhi and Ibn Jarir also transmit it.
rows.anchor: لسرادق النار أربعة جدر، كثافة كل جدار مسافة أربعين سنة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas defines Hell's enclosure as a wall of fire, in a report from Ibn Jurayj.
rows.anchor: [وقال ابن جريج: قال ابن عباس: {أحاط بهم سرادقها} قال: حائط من نار]

rows.speaker: يعلى بن أمية
rows.claim: Ya'la reports that the Prophet called the sea Hell, then recited this verse when asked how, and swore he would never enter it while alive or be touched by a drop of it.
rows.anchor: عن يعلى بن أمية قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "البحر هو جهنم"

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas describes muhl as thick liquid like the dregs of oil.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: "المهل": ماء غليظ مثل

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says muhl is like blood and pus.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: هو كالدم والقيح.

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima says muhl is something whose heat has reached its limit.
rows.anchor: وقال عكرمة: هو الشيء الذي انتهى حره

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Other authorities interpret muhl as anything melted.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون: هو كل شيء أذيب.

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says Ibn Masud melted gold in a trench; once it liquefied and foamed, he called it the closest likeness of muhl.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: أذاب ابن مسعود شيئا من الذهب في أخدود، فلما انماع وأزبد قال: هذا أشبه شيء بالمهل.

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says Hell's water is black because Hell is black and its people are black.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك: ماء جهنم أسود، وهي سوداء وأهلها (1) سود.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These descriptions do not conflict: muhl combines the repulsive traits of being black, foul, thick, and hot.
rows.anchor: فإن المهل يجمع هذه الأوصاف الرذيلة كلها، فهو أسود منتن غليظ حار

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet explains that muhl is like oil sediment and that bringing it near makes the face's skin fall into it; Tirmidhi says this route is only known through Rashdin, criticized for memory, while Ahmad transmits it through Ibn Lahi'a.
rows.anchor: عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال: "ماء كالمهل". قال (2) كعكر الزيت

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: In a report explaining 14:16–17, Abu Umama says the drink is brought near unwillingly, burns the face and removes the scalp, then cuts the drinker's intestines.
rows.anchor: عن أبي أمامة، رضي الله عنه، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في قوله: {ويسقى من ماء صديد يتجرعه}

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr says the people of Hell eat Zaqqum when hungry, losing their facial skin, then cry for water and receive muhl so hot that the remaining flesh on their faces is scorched near their mouths.
rows.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير: إذا جاع أهل النار استغاثوا بشجرة الزقوم، فأكلوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The muhl drink is vile and scalding, like the hot water of 47:15 and 88:5; the spring called aniy is intensely hot, as in 55:44.
rows.anchor: القبيحة: {بئس الشراب} أي: بئس هذا الشراب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fire is a wretched place to lodge, rest, gather, or seek comfort, like the bad abode and residence described in 25:66.
rows.anchor: منزلا ومقيلا ومجتمعا وموضعا للارتفاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believer's question rebukes the garden owner for denying the God who created him from dust through Adam and then from a drop of humble fluid; the statement affirms God's sole lordship and worship.
rows.anchor: وهذا إنكار وتعظيم لما وقع فيه من جحود ربه، الذي خلقه وابتدأ خلق الإنسان من طين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As 2:280 asks how people can disbelieve after being lifeless and brought to life, everyone knows they once did not exist and could not create themselves or derive existence from another created thing; this plainly points to God as Creator.
rows.anchor: فإنه ما من أحد من المخلوقات إلا ويعلم أنه كان معدوما ثم وجد، وليس وجوده من نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The garden owner should have praised God on seeing what delighted him, acknowledging that God granted him exceptional wealth and children and that there is no power except through God.
rows.anchor: هلا إذا أعجبتك حين دخلتها ونظرت إليها حمدت الله على ما أنعم به عليك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some early authorities advise saying God willing, no power except through God when impressed by one's condition, possessions, or children, deriving the counsel from this verse.
rows.anchor: قال بعض السلف: من أعجبه شيء من حاله أو ماله

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A report from Anas says that when a servant says God willing, no power except through God, over a blessing of family, wealth, or children, he will see no calamity in it short of death; Abu Ya'la transmits it.
rows.anchor: نعمة من أهل أو مال أو ولد، فيقول: {ما شاء الله لا قوة إلا بالله}

rows.speaker: أبو الفتح الأزدي
rows.claim: Al-Azdi says the Anas report through Isa ibn Awn and Abd al-Malik ibn Zarara is not sound.
rows.anchor: قال الحافظ أبو الفتح الأزدي: عيسى بن عون، عن عبد الملك بن زرارة

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: The Prophet called the phrase no power except through God a treasure from the Garden; Ahmad alone transmits this report.
rows.anchor: ألا أدلك على كنز من كنوز الجنة؟ لا قوة إلا بالله

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: In an authentic report to Abu Musa, the Prophet calls there is no might or power except through God a treasure of the Garden.
rows.anchor: ألا أدلك على كنز من كنوز الجنة؟ لا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra distinguishes the treasure under the Throne as the phrase no power except through God, and says this is the wording in the Cave verse, unlike no might or power except through God.
rows.anchor: فقال: لا إنها في سورة الكهف: {ولولا إذ دخلت جنتك قلت ما شاء الله لا قوة إلا بالله}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The orchard owner's fruits, or his wealth by another interpretation, were surrounded by ruin: the disaster the believer had warned about struck the garden that had distracted him from God.
rows.anchor: بأمواله، أو بثماره على القول الآخر.

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada explains turning the hands as clapping them in grief and regret for the wealth he had spent and lost.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: يصفق كفيه متأسفا متلهفا على الأموال التي أذهبها عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His clan or children, whom he had boasted in, could not support him; he could not save himself, and at that moment true authority belonged to God.
rows.anchor: أي: عشيرة أو ولد، كما افتخر بهم واستعز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Readers differ in where to pause: some stop after the clause that he had no victory there, then begin that authority belongs to God; others pause after no victory and begin with there belongs the authority.
rows.anchor: اختلف القراء هاهنا، فمنهم من يقف على قوله: {وما كان منتصرا هنالك}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With an open initial waw in al-walaya, the meaning is allegiance to God: when punishment comes, everyone, believer or unbeliever, returns to Him in submission, as Pharaoh and others did (40:84; 10:90–91).
rows.anchor: من مؤمن أو كافر (7) يرجع إلى الله وإلى موالاته والخضوع له إذا وقع العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With a kasra on the waw, al-wilaya means that judgment belongs to God alone.
rows.anchor: ومنهم من كسر الواو من {الولاية} أي: هنالك الحكم لله الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Readers also differ grammatically: raising al-haqq makes it an adjective of authority, as in 25:26; lowering its final qaf makes it an adjective of God, as in 6:62.
rows.anchor: ثم منهم من رفع {الحق} على أنه نعت للولاية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gives the best reward and outcome: deeds done for Him earn a better reward and a sound, wholly good end.
rows.anchor: الأعمال التي تكون لله، عز وجل، ثوابها خير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly life fades like rain-fed vegetation: it grows and becomes beautiful, then dries into fragments scattered in every direction by the wind; God has power over both states and everything else.
rows.anchor: يابسا {تذروه الرياح} أي: تفرقه وتطرحه ذات اليمين وذات الشمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same fleeting-life image appears in the parables of 10:24, 39:21, and 57:20; an authentic hadith also calls the world sweet and green.
rows.anchor: وكثيرا ما يضرب الله مثل الحياة الدنيا بهذا المثل كما في سورة يونس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wealth and children adorn worldly life (3:14), but assets and offspring are a trial (64:15); turning to God and worshipping Him is better than being occupied with them, collecting more, or excessively worrying for them.
rows.anchor: الإقبال عليه والتفرغ لعبادته، خير لكم من اشتغالكم بهم والجمع لهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وسعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, and other early authorities identify the lasting righteous deeds as the five daily prayers.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس، وسعيد بن جبير، وغير واحد من السلف: "الباقيات الصالحات" الصلوات الخمس

rows.speaker: عطاء بن أبي رباح وسعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Another report from Ata and Sa'id, citing Ibn Abbas, identifies them as the formulas: glory be to God, praise be to God, no deity but God, and God is greatest.
rows.anchor: وقال عطاء بن أبي رباح، وسعيد بن جبير، عن ابن عباس: "الباقيات الصالحات" سبحان الله

rows.speaker: عثمان بن عفان
rows.claim: Uthman says they are the four remembrance formulas plus no might or power except through God; in Ahmad's report he explains this after describing forgiveness through the five prayers.
rows.anchor: فقال: هي (5) لا إله إلا الله، وسبحان الله، والحمد لله

rows.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
rows.claim: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib identifies the lasting deeds as the four remembrance formulas plus no might or power except through God.
rows.anchor: قال: "الباقيات الصالحات" سبحان الله، والحمد لله، ولا إله إلا الله، والله أكبر

rows.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
rows.claim: When offered prayer and fasting, then zakat and pilgrimage, Sa'id rejects both lists and says the five lasting formulas are the four remembrances plus no might or power except through God.
rows.anchor: قال (6) لم تصب. فقلت: الزكاة والحج. فقال: لم تصب، ولكنهن الكلمات الخمس

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn Umar identifies them as no deity but God, God is greatest, glory be to God, and no might or power except through God; Ata is reported to give the same answer.
rows.anchor: أنه سأل ابن عمر عن: {الباقيات الصالحات} قال: لا إله إلا الله، والله أكبر

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid identifies them as glory be to God, praise be to God, no deity but God, and God is greatest.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: {الباقيات الصالحات} سبحان الله، والحمد لله، ولا إله إلا الله، والله أكبر

rows.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
rows.claim: Hasan and Qatada give the four formulas: no deity but God, God is greatest, praise be to God, and glory be to God.
rows.anchor: وقال عبد الرزاق: أخبرنا معمر، عن الحسن وقتادة في قوله: "الباقيات الصالحات"

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A report from Abu Hurayra says that glory be to God, praise be to God, no deity but God, and God is greatest are among the lasting righteous deeds; Ibn Jarir transmits it.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "سبحان الله، والحمد لله، ولا إله إلا الله، والله أكبر، من الباقيات الصالحات"

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet urges people to increase the lasting righteous deeds; asked what they are, he names the religion and explains it as magnifying, declaring God's oneness, glorifying and praising Him, and saying no might or power except through God.
rows.anchor: قيل: وما هي (9) يا رسول الله؟ قال: "الملة"

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Ahmad also transmits the Prophet's report, through Darraj, that people should increase the lasting righteous deeds and that they are the formulas of remembrance.
rows.anchor: وهكذا رواه أحمد، من حديث دراج، به (10) .

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn Ka'b includes no might or power except through God among the lasting deeds; Salim questions its inclusion, but Muhammad persists, and Salim confirms after citing Abu Ayyub's report that Abraham told the Prophet to teach the community this as a seed of Paradise because its soil is good and broad.
rows.anchor: فقال: لا إله إلا الله، وسبحان الله، والله أكبر، ولا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A report from Abu Ayyub says that during the heavenly ascent Abraham urged the Prophet to tell his community to plant abundantly in Paradise, explaining that its planting is no might or power except through God.
rows.anchor: فأريت إبراهيم عليه السلام، فقال: يا جبريل من هذا معك؟

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A report from an unnamed man of the Ansar says the Prophet warned that supporting unjust rulers and believing their lies disowns one from him, while refusing both aligns one with him; he then names four remembrance formulas as the lasting righteous deeds.
rows.anchor: خرج علينا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، ونحن في المسجد بعد صلاة العشاء

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet names four remembrance formulas and a parent who loses a righteous child and seeks God's reward among five weighty deeds; he also names five beliefs with which one meets God and enters Paradise: God, the Last Day, Paradise, Hell, resurrection, and reckoning.
rows.anchor: بخ بخ لخمس ما أثقلهن في الميزان: لا إله إلا الله، والله أكبر

rows.speaker: شداد بن أوس
rows.claim: Shaddad regrets asking his servant for a knife to play with, saying that since embracing Islam he had controlled every word except that one; he relays the Prophet's counsel to treasure a supplication for steadfastness, resolve in guidance, gratitude, worship, a sound heart and truthful tongue, good known to God, refuge from known evil, and forgiveness, when others hoard gold and silver. Ahmad and al-Nasa'i transmit it.
rows.anchor: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: "إذا كنز الناس الذهب والفضة فاكنزوا (14) هؤلاء الكلمات

rows.speaker: سعد بن جنادة
rows.claim: Sa'd ibn Janadah says that after he first came to the Prophet from Taif and converted, the Prophet taught him the four remembrance formulas as lasting righteous deeds; al-Tabarani transmits it.
rows.anchor: وعلمني هؤلاء الكلمات: سبحان الله، والحمد لله، ولا إله إلا الله، والله أكبر

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A report through Sa'd ibn Janadah says that one who rises at night, performs ablution and rinses his mouth, then says each of the four formulas one hundred times is forgiven all sins except bloodshed.
rows.anchor: من قام من الليل فتوضأ ومضمض فاه، ثم قال: سبحان الله مائة مرة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas gives a broad list of lasting deeds: remembrance, blessings on the Prophet, fasting, prayer, pilgrimage, charity, freeing slaves, jihad, maintaining kinship, and all good works, which remain for their people in Paradise as long as heaven and earth endure.
rows.anchor: هي ذكر الله، قول: لا إله إلا الله، والله أكبر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Awfi transmits Ibn Abbas's interpretation of the lasting righteous deeds as good speech.
rows.anchor: وقال العوفي، عن ابن عباس: هن الكلام الطيب.

rows.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم
rows.claim: Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam says they are all righteous deeds; Ibn Jarir chooses this broad interpretation.
rows.anchor: وقال عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم: هي الأعمال الصالحة كلها. واختاره ابن جرير

rows.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص
rows.claim: Asked whether the greatest losers are the Haruriyya, Sa'd answers that they are Jews and Christians: Jews rejected Muhammad, while Christians denied food and drink in Paradise; the Haruriyya break God's covenant after pledging it, and Sa'd called them profligates. Bukhari transmits this.
rows.anchor: سألت أبي -يعني سعد بن أبي وقاص-: {قل هل ننبئكم بالأخسرين أعمالا} أهم الحرورية؟ قال: لا هم اليهود والنصارى

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب والضحاك
rows.claim: Ali, al-Dahhak, and others identify the greatest losers as the Haruriyya.
rows.anchor: وقال علي بن أبي طالب (1) والضحاك، وغير واحد: هم الحرورية.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse broadly includes the Haruriyya alongside Jews, Christians, and others; it is not exclusive to any group, since it is Meccan, before the relevant Jewish-Christian address and before the Khawarij existed. It covers anyone who follows an unapproved way while thinking the work is accepted, as echoed in 88:2–4, 25:23, and 24:39.
rows.anchor: أن هذه الآية الكريمة تشمل الحرورية كما تشمل اليهود والنصارى وغيرهم، لا أنها نزلت في هؤلاء على الخصوص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The greatest losers are those whose efforts were invalid under a lawful, pleasing religious way, yet who believe they are doing well and that their deeds are accepted and loved.
rows.anchor: أي: عملوا أعمالا باطلة على غير شريعة مشروعة مرضية مقبولة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God plants affection for believers who perform righteous deeds pleasing to Him by following Muhammad's law in the hearts of righteous people; this is certain and unavoidable.
rows.anchor: يغرس لهم في قلوب عباده الصالحين مودة، وهذا أمر لا بد منه

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: When God loves a servant, He tells Gabriel, who loves him and announces God's love among heaven's inhabitants; they love him, and acceptance is placed for him on earth. God does the inverse for one He hates. The report is transmitted by Ahmad and Muslim from Abu Hurayra, with parallel routes in Ahmad and Bukhari.
rows.anchor: إن الله إذا أحب عبدا دعا جبريل فقال: يا جبريل، إني أحب فلانا فأحبه

rows.speaker: ثوبان
rows.claim: Thawban reports that a servant seeking God's pleasure receives God's mercy; Gabriel, the Throne-bearers, those around them, and the inhabitants of the seven heavens invoke mercy for him, which then descends to earth. Ibn Kathir calls this route rare and says the compilers did not transmit it.
rows.anchor: إن العبد ليلتمس مرضات (6) الله، فلا يزال كذلك (7)

rows.speaker: أبو أمامة
rows.claim: A report says God's love is announced in heaven and descends to earth, while hatred is likewise announced and spreads through earth; Sharik glosses al-miqah as love. Ibn Kathir calls the route rare and says the compilers did not transmit it.
rows.anchor: عن أبي أمامة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: In a report from Abu Hurayra, God tells Gabriel He loves a servant, Gabriel announces this in heaven, and love is then placed for the servant among earth's people; Muslim and Tirmidhi transmit it, and Tirmidhi grades it hasan sahih.
rows.anchor: أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "إذا أحب الله عبدا نادى جبريل: إني قد أحببت فلانا، فأحبه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses God's granting wuddan as love; Mujahid reports from him that it means love among people in this world.
rows.anchor: وقال علي بن أبي طلحة، عن ابن عباس في قوله: {سيجعل لهم الرحمن ودا} قال: حبا.

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr says God loves these believers and makes believing people love them; Mujahid, al-Dahhak, and others give the same interpretation.
rows.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير، عنه: يحبهم ويحببهم، يعني: إلى خلقه المؤمنين.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Awfi transmits Ibn Abbas's broader explanation of wuddan as Muslims' affection in this world, good provision, and an honest reputation.
rows.anchor: وقال العوفي، عن ابن عباس أيضا: الود من المسلمين في الدنيا، والرزق الحسن، واللسان الصادق.

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says God places this affection in believers' hearts; Hurm ibn Hayyan said that when a servant turns his heart to God, God turns believing hearts toward him and grants their love and mercy.
rows.anchor: في قلوب أهل الإيمان، ذكر (2) لنا أن هرم بن حيان كان يقول

rows.speaker: عثمان بن عفان
rows.claim: Uthman said that God clothes every person in the mantle of whatever deed, good or evil, that person performs.
rows.anchor: وكان عثمان بن عفان، رضي الله عنه، يقول: ما من عبد يعمل خيرا، أو شرا

rows.speaker: الحسن البصري
rows.claim: Hasan tells of a man who worshipped conspicuously for seven months without gaining respect; when he redirected the same deeds to God alone, people began to pray for mercy on him. Hasan recited this verse about him.
rows.anchor: فلم يزد على أن (3) قلب نيته، ولم يزد على العمل الذي كان يعمله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deniers are asked whether the destroyed peoples before them have taught them a lesson: they vanished without trace, leaving empty dwellings through which people walk. Sound-minded people should take the signs, as in 22:46 and 32:26.
rows.anchor: كم أهلكنا من الأمم المكذبين بالرسل قبلهم، فبادوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A prior divine decree delays punishment until proof has been established, and a term was set for these deniers; otherwise punishment would have come suddenly.
rows.anchor: لا يعذب أحدا إلا بعد قيام الحجة عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is consoled to endure their denials; glorifying God before sunrise and sunset means the dawn and afternoon prayers. In an authentic report, Jarir says the Prophet compared seeing God to seeing the full moon and urged guarding those prayers.
rows.anchor: فإن استطعتم ألا تغلبوا على صلاة قبل طلوع الشمس وقبل غروبها، فافعلوا

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet said that no one who performs prayer before sunrise and before sunset will enter the Fire; Muslim transmits the report from Umara ibn Ruwayba.
rows.anchor: لن يلج النار أحد صلى قبل طلوع الشمس وقبل غروبها

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A report from Ibn Umar says the lowest person in Paradise sees a kingdom stretching a thousand years, while the highest in rank sees God twice each day.
rows.anchor: إن أدنى أهل الجنة منزلة من ينظر في ملكه مسيرة ألف سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The night intervals mean its hours and the night prayer; some instead interpret them as the sunset and night prayers. The day's ends correspond to the night intervals.
rows.anchor: وقوله: {ومن آناء الليل فسبح} أي: من ساعاته فتهجد به. وحمله بعضهم على المغرب والعشاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hope of contentment recalls God's promise to give until the Prophet is pleased in 93:5.
rows.anchor: كما قال تعالى: {ولسوف يعطيك ربك فترضى} [الضحى: 5]

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: In an authentic report, God asks the people of Paradise if they are satisfied; after they cite His unmatched gifts, He promises them His pleasure and says He will never be displeased with them.
rows.anchor: أحل عليكم رضواني، فلا أسخط عليكم بعده أبدا

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Another report says that after people of Paradise recall that God whitened their faces, weighted their scales, saved them from the Fire, and admitted them to Paradise, the veil is lifted and seeing God proves a greater gift, called the increase.
rows.anchor: فوالله ما أعطاهم خيرا من النظر إليه، وهي (5) الزيادة

rows.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة
rows.claim: Mujahid, Qatada, and others interpret worshipping God on an edge as worship based on doubt.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد، وقتادة، وغيرهما: {على حرف}

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Others take the phrase literally as being on an edge, like a mountain's rim: a person enters religion conditionally, staying if things go well and withdrawing otherwise.
rows.anchor: وقال غيرهم: على طرف. ومنه حرف الجبل، أي: طرفه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas describes a man arriving in Medina who judges the religion good if his wife bears a son and his horses produce foals, but bad if neither occurs; Bukhari transmits it.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس {ومن الناس من يعبد الله على حرف} قال: كان الرجل يقدم المدينة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Another report says Bedouins accepted Islam with the Prophet, then judged it good in years of rain, plenty, and healthy births, but worthless in drought and poor births; this was the occasion for the verse.
rows.anchor: كان ناس من الأعراب يأتون النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فيسلمون، فإذا رجعوا إلى بلادهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Awfi's account says Medina's fever, a daughter rather than a son, or delayed charity could make a new convert think his religion brought only harm; this is the trial meant here. Qatada, al-Dahhak, Ibn Jurayj, and other early authorities give the same basic explanation.
rows.anchor: وقال العوفي، عن ابن عباس: كان أحدهم إذا قدم المدينة، وهي أرض وبيئة

rows.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd interprets the person as a hypocrite who worships only while worldly affairs prosper, then abandons worship and returns to disbelief when hardship or a test comes.
rows.anchor: هو المنافق، إن صلحت له دنياه أقام على العبادة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid explains turning back on one's face as apostatizing into disbelief.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد في قوله: {انقلب على وجهه} أي: ارتد كافرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wavering worshipper gains nothing in this life and has rejected God for the next, suffering the clearest and greatest loss.
rows.anchor: أي: فلا هو حصل من الدنيا على شيء، وأما الآخرة فقد كفر بالله العظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who invoke idols and rivals seek help, victory, and provision from things that neither harm nor benefit; their harm in this world is nearer than any benefit, and in the next it is certain.
rows.anchor: أي: من الأصنام والأنداد، يستغيث بها ويستنصرها ويسترزقها، وهي لا تنفعه ولا تضره

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the bad protector and bad companion are the idol being invoked.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد: يعني الوثن، يعني: بئس هذا الذي دعا به من دون الله مولى

rows.speaker: ابن جرير
rows.claim: Ibn Jarir instead takes the bad protector and companion to mean a bad paternal cousin or associate: the person who worships only while worldly conditions suit him.
rows.anchor: واختار ابن جرير أن المراد: لبئس ابن العم والصاحب من يعبد [الله] (2) على حرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir prefers Mujahid's reading of the bad protector and companion as an idol because it better fits the flow of the passage.
rows.anchor: وقول مجاهد: إن المراد به الوثن، أولى وأقرب إلى سياق الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At death, unbelievers and those who neglected God's commands ask to return to worldly life so they can repair what they ruined; they are refused. The same plea appears in 63:10–11, 14:44, 7:53, 32:12, 6:27–28, 42:44, 40:11–12, and 35:37.
rows.anchor: يخبر تعالى عن حال المحتضر عند الموت، من الكافرين أو المفرطين في أمر الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are denied a return at the moment of death, at resurrection, during judgment before the Lord, and when shown the Fire; they remain amid the throes of Hell's punishment.
rows.anchor: فذكر تعالى أنهم يسألون الرجعة، فلا يجابون، عند الاحتضار، ويوم النشور ووقت العرض على الجبار
